text: 3M is a diversified technology company with a global presence in safety and industrial; transportation and electronics; and consumer markets. We manage our operations in three business segments and sell products in approximately 200 countries. Our safety and industrial segment supplies personal safety equipment, abrasives, adhesives, tapes and roofing granules. Our transportation and electronics segment supplies films, display materials and aerospace products. Our consumer segment supplies home care, stationery and home improvement products under brands including Post-it, Scotch, Filtrete and Command. We completed the exit of all per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance manufacturing by the end of 2025 and continue to work to discontinue the use of PFAS across our product portfolio, a programme that has required reformulation of a number of product lines and the closure or conversion of several manufacturing sites.

We are exposed to significant environmental, product liability and other claims. Our exit from PFAS manufacturing does not resolve claims arising from historical manufacturing or from the presence of these substances in the environment, and we continue to face claims by public water systems, state attorneys general and individuals alleging property damage, remediation costs and personal injury. The cost of remediating sites where PFAS were manufactured or disposed of, and the cost of defending and resolving these claims, could exceed the amounts we have accrued. We are also subject to ongoing regulatory requirements relating to discharges to water and air at our facilities, and from time to time we have been in non-compliance with permit limits. New drinking water standards for PFAS adopted in several jurisdictions may increase both the number of claimants and the scope of remediation sought from us.

The Company is a defendant in numerous proceedings relating to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances. In June 2023 the Company entered into a settlement with public water systems in the United States, under which it agreed to pay up to $12.5 billion through 2036 to fund testing and treatment of PFAS in drinking water. Separately, the Company has resolved claims brought by service members alleging hearing damage from Combat Arms earplugs for an aggregate of $6.0 billion payable through 2029. Attorneys general in 32 states have filed natural resource damage actions that are not covered by the public water system settlement, and the Company is a defendant in personal injury actions alleging that exposure to PFAS caused kidney cancer, thyroid disease and ulcerative colitis. The Company has accrued $3.1 billion for these matters, which does not reflect amounts for claims it cannot reasonably estimate.

On June 11, 2026, 3M Company reached an agreement in principle with the attorneys general of four states to resolve natural resource damage claims relating to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances for an aggregate of $825 million, payable over eight years. The agreement is subject to definitive documentation and court approval and does not resolve claims brought by other states, by individual plaintiffs, or claims relating to the Company's Cordova, Illinois facility. The Company expects to record a pre-tax charge of $825 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Water companies say the clean-up bill for PFAS contamination will run well past the end of the payment schedules agreed with manufacturers, because treatment plants installed to remove the chemicals have to be operated and have their filters replaced for decades. One utility serving 1.2 million people said settlement money covers roughly 60% of its capital cost and none of its operating cost. 3M, which agreed in 2023 to pay up to $12.5 billion to public water systems and this week settled natural resource claims with four states, said it has exited PFAS manufacturing and is working with utilities on treatment technology. Environmental lawyers said the pattern of settling state by state means the company's total exposure will not be known for years, which is the point charities screening for pollution litigation tend to find hardest to price.

EPA ECHO detailed facility report for 3M Cordova, Illinois (NPDES permit IL0000426) records the facility in significant non-compliance for two of the twelve most recent quarters, with effluent limit exceedances reported for perfluorooctanoic acid and total suspended solids. One formal enforcement action is listed with a penalty of $132,000 assessed in the current reporting period, and the facility remains under a compliance schedule for outfall monitoring. Name match to the registered facility operator was exact. Air and hazardous waste programmes at the site show no violations in the same period.

3M raised its full-year adjusted earnings guidance after organic sales grew 3.4% in the second quarter, led by industrial adhesives and aerospace. Adjusted operating margin expanded 180 basis points year on year. The company said the $825 million natural resource damage agreement announced in June is reflected in reported results but excluded from adjusted figures, and that it continues to expect PFAS-related cash payments of roughly $1.2 billion a year through 2029.
